top_signal.title: 8 years in business, 40+ products I designed, Fortune 500 buyers — and I can't get a line of credit because I bootstrapped on personal cards. Need advice.
top_signal.summary: I'm going to lay this all out with real numbers because every financing post on here is vague and I want real advice, not generic answers.   I own a small manufacturing company in New Jersey. We design and build laboratory testing instruments from the ground up — mechanical, electrical, and software. We're not assembling other people's stuff or reselling anything. We design our own machines, build them in-house, and sell direct to end users and distributors worldwide. Over 8 years we've developed about 40 different machines and our catalog has about 480 SKUs (instruments, glassware, accessories).   Our customers include Fortune 500 energy companies, national labs, and international distributors. Not naming them here, but these are companies everyone has heard of. They're repeat buyers on purchase orders — not leads in a CRM, actual customers that keep coming back.    TL;DR:  8-year NJ manufacturer of lab testing instruments. 40+ machines I designed from scratch, Fortune 500 customers, ~$500K–$800K/yr revenue, 87% gross margins, $414K in current bookings. Built the whole thing on credit cards which killed my credit score (high 500s). That locked me out of normal lending and pushed me into an MCA which made everything worse. Tariffs disrupted our supply chain in 2025 and the cash flow effects are still hitting. Sitting on $17K cash, ~$90K in credit card debt, ~$55K left on the MCA, ~$15K on a QB LOC, and ~$133K in payroll tax liability. Our bank has already said they'd give us
